info.title: Screeps World HTTP API
info.summary: Source-derived contract of the official Screeps World (screeps.com) HTTP API
info.description: Community-maintained contract of the official Screeps World HTTP API at https://screeps.com, not published by Screeps. Evidence: static analysis of the official web client assets (pinned by bust and SHA-256 in coverage.json), the community client node-screeps-api and the official private-server source screeps/backend-local, all pinned in sources.json/coverage.json and cited per operation in x-sources. `x-availability['screeps-com']` is `supported` when official evidence shows the operation is used against screeps.com, `unverified` otherwise; `x-unverified` states known evidence gaps. A supported marker does not mean every operation was exercised live. The official web client treats a response as successful only when the JSON body has a truthy `ok`; logical failures arrive as `{error}` usually with HTTP 200, so never infer success from the status code. Signed-in requests send `X-Token` (and the legacy `X-Username` with the same value); a returned `X-Token` response header replaces the stored token. The client may also send `X-Ignore-Server-Down: 1`. Standalone/private servers are described by the separate standalone compatibility profile (profiles/standalone.json), not by this document. WebSocket/SockJS channels and the in-game JavaScript API are outside this document. Endpoints can have destructive effects; examples are not authorization to invoke them.

servers.description: Official Screeps World; `shard` query/body fields route shard-specific operations.

externalDocs.description: Pinned source provenance, coverage and the standalone compatibility profile

Token.name: X-Token
Token.description: Official API auth token or session token. Servers may return a rotated token in the X-Token response header; store it for subsequent requests. Never send tokens to untrusted hosts or follow authenticated cross-host redirects.

Shard.name: shard
Shard.description: Official shard routing for operations that accept it (for example `shard3`).

LegacyUsername.name: X-Username
LegacyUsername.description: Legacy header: the official web client sends the token value here as well as in X-Token.

ServerError.description: Server failed to process the request.

Success.description: Success or a logical API failure; inspect the body even when HTTP status is 200.

JsonValue.description: Arbitrary JSON value deliberately unconstrained (for example user-owned Memory).
